recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-16469 follow-up is needed unless a later final vocabulary decision changes the still-open example/fragment policy questions.
issue_request: FHIR-16469 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 vocabulary issue asking FHIR-core CodeSystem content mode definitions to distinguish example from fragment. The approved clarification said example content has no useful subset intent and is not intended to be workable, while fragment content is a curated subset released for a purpose with the intent, bounds, and consequences of fragmentation clearly documented.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 14680, represented in git by 54cd02036599308b033f2838d80f5b7d842daf33, which updated the old source/codesystem/codesystem-spreadsheet.xml definitions for example and fragment.
additional_context: The source has since been refactored into active CodeSystem and ValueSet XML. Later decisions FHIR-39163 and FHIR-51110 refined the example definition, while FHIR-33947 refined the fragment definition and retained the original intent/bounds/consequences requirement in the Code System Fragments narrative. FHIR-27147 rejected adding a separate subset mode; FHIR-53375 and FHIR-48959 remain later unresolved or not-yet-applied context and do not change this seed decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source says example is an illustrative subset with no specific purpose or documented intent and should not be used when fragment is the better representation; fragment is a curated subset released for a specific purpose; and the fragment narrative requires intent, bounds, and consequences to be clearly defined.
